newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland sees rapid growth, no inflation pressures.
newsitem.headline: Finland sees rapid growth, no inflation pressures.

text.p: The Finnish finance ministry said in an economic bulletin received on Wednesday that recent data showed ongoing rapid growth, but no inflation pressures.
"The recent data on the Finnish economy point to continued rapid growth with no inflationary pressures," the ministry said in the bulletin dated January 21.
"Industrial output is expanding rapidly and the situation is improving markedly also in construction," it said.
"Confidence is healthy both in the business and household sectors, demand for credit is picking up and sentiment is optimistic in the Helsinki Stock Exchange," the ministry said.

The bulletin did not contain a new forecast. Martti Hetemaki, head of the ministry's economics department has said it is likely that the ministry will upgrade its 3.9 percent 1997 GDP growth forecast from September in the next forecast due in February.
In the new bulletin, the ministry said the decline in unemployment had been slow.
"The number of jobs is rising, but so is also the supply of labour. Thus, the decline in the unemployment rate has remained rather slow," it said.

The rise in the December jobless rate -- to 19.0 percent from 17.4 percent in November -- reported by the labour ministry last week was "obviously due to changes in the unemployment benefits as from January 1, which caused a surge in registrations for unemployment", the finance ministry said.
